body: This is stale after the swap from the `Callable` approach

This happened because I didn't know how to properly get `TextEdit` and `CodePos` exposed to scripting, and `add_code_completion_option` is available to scripting. The ClassDB bind methods are unable to handle the extra default argument, so the original `add_code_completion_option` became a bouncer to this method.

Another mental TODO here is that this currently applies each time for a multi-caret completion.

Given that the positions in `ScriptLanguage::TextEdit` are absolute, and are not aware of the fact that a completion could be used for multiple carets, we might want to only apply them once after all carets have completed

https://i.imgur.com/9liZOSc.mp4

I'm going to resolve this for now and consider the multi-caret usage here undefined behavior. Autofilling multiple functions isn't supported anyway (as function names must not be duplicated). If we relax function names to function signatures at some point maybe we can reconsider.

I think this isn't a good situation in our codebase with code duplication (you're essentially looking up a class that's already found in `get_function_signature()`). Perhaps we could replace the `StringName *r_native_class` parameter so that it returns the name of the class in which the method is defined, regardless of whether it's native or not.
Perhaps `is_marked_as_override` sounds better?
I think this is a very unfortunate naming, considering that we already have a `TextEdit` control.

body: Thank you for trying to document the code thoroughly, but I'm not sure we have a consensus on this. The use of large comments and JavaDoc tags only in a few places is inconsistent.
I haven't reviewed the editor's changes, but are they really necessary? Couldn't we postpone them for a follow-up PR?

It is a little bit unfortunate but it isn't being driven by us. The upstream LSP name is [`TextEdit`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textEdit). If we want to avoid collisions we could call this `LSPTextEdit`.

I think the usability of this feature is severely diminished without the editor changes included. The editor changes already went through a fairly good round of discussion earlier in the PR's lifecycle.

Basically if we removed the editor changes then we'd need to also remove the warnings or downgrade the warnings to disabled-by-default until the editor changes make it in. Otherwise it's a chore that you have to manually type `@override` on every new overridden method.

We do apparently use this style of docs in some places, most notably the `gdextension_interface.h` (although it has now been replaced with a `.json` in canon).

I do absolutely think the codebase is undercommented, and people should add comments where necessary to understand the code.

Hm, yeah. Changing it to `int line = ctx.current_line - 1;` resolves all those issues. Not really sure why though.
It comes from the tokenizer, which tracks line and column numbers as displayed in the editor and error messages, so one-based. That's my understanding anyway.
I realized I can't actually impose the restriction for `@abstract` since a grandchild may redeclare a function as abstract, which will then require an `@override`.
I was able to augment `get_function_signature()` to return the declaring class. Using that allows removing this hunk.
